The diagram shown above is the slope field for which of the following differential equations?
worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14044310/assets/d7f1fccf2bb73f160faa04c058db6892f78f105e374516c97558f81121fc49f8.png)

 

Notice the following properties of the given slope field:

- First, the slopes of the slope field are horizontal along the lines $x=0$ and $x=2.$ Therefore, the right-hand side of the differential equation should equal zero on both of these lines.

Of the given equations, the only equations that satisfy this condition are the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & ={x}^{2}(2-x) \\ {y}^{′} & =x(x-2)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

- Second, the lines $x=0$ and $x=2$ divide the plane into $3$ regions. The sign of the slopes in each of the $3$ regions are easily deduced by considering the behavior of the solution curves in these regions. This information is summarized in the following table:

| Region | $x<0$ | $0<x<2$ | $x>2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Slope | $↗$ | $↗$ | $↘$ |
| Sign | $+$ | $+$ | $-$ |

Of the three remaining options, the only one that gives this behavior is

$$
{y}^{′}={x}^{2}(2-x).
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is ${y}^{′}={x}^{2}(2-x).$
